title: Basic Temporal and Modal Prepositions
summary: Everyday prepositions such as in, vor, nach, mit, and ohne in common expressions.
whyItMatters: Prepositions connect events to time and actions to their circumstances. At this level, a small set of reliable chunks lets you say when something happens, what happens before or after another event, and whether you travel or act with or without something.

mentalModel.title: Time prepositions place events on a line
mentalModel.content: Use 'vor' for before, 'nach' for after, and 'in' for a future interval or a period: vor dem Kurs, nach der Arbeit, in einer Stunde.

mentalModel.title: Modal prepositions describe how
mentalModel.content: Use 'mit' to include a means, person, or tool and 'ohne' to exclude one: mit dem Bus, mit Anna, ohne Auto.

mentalModel.title: Learn the preposition with its case
mentalModel.content: Treat each pattern as a package: mit + dative, nach + dative, vor + dative, in + dative for these time expressions, and ohne + accusative.

ruleBlocks.title: Use in for a future interval
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'in' with the dative to say how long from now: in einer Stunde, in zwei Tagen, in einer Woche.

ruleBlocks.title: Use vor and nach around events
ruleBlocks.content: Use dative chunks such as 'vor dem Termin', 'vor der Arbeit', 'nach dem Kurs', and 'nach der Pause'.

ruleBlocks.title: Use mit for company, tools, and transport
ruleBlocks.content: 'Mit' always takes the dative: mit dem Bus, mit der Bahn, mit einem Stadtplan, mit Freunden.

ruleBlocks.title: Use ohne for what is absent
ruleBlocks.content: 'Ohne' takes the accusative: ohne den Stadtplan, ohne eine Fahrkarte, ohne mein Handy.

patterns: nach der Arbeit / vor dem Kurs
sentenceStructure: A prepositional phrase can appear in the middle or at the beginning of a sentence.
When the phrase comes first, the conjugated verb remains in position two: 'Nach dem Kurs fahre ich nach Hause.'
The preposition determines the article form in these patterns.
Plural dative nouns often add '-n' when possible: mit den Freunden.

concepts: use in, vor, and nach in common time expressions
use mit plus dative and ohne plus accusative
use a broader range of temporal and modal prepositions
distinguish location and direction with two-way prepositions
choose precise prepositions in abstract and idiomatic contexts
manage complex time relationships across clauses

comparisons.summary: The city lesson supplies concrete transport and schedule contexts for 'mit', 'ohne', 'vor', and 'nach'.
Help exchanges use these chunks to explain timing and means: 'Ich komme in fünf Minuten' or 'Wir fahren mit dem Bus'.

rows: Ja, aber mit dem Handy ist es leichter.

examples.de: Der Bus kommt in zehn Minuten.
examples.en: The bus is coming in ten minutes.

examples.de: Wir treffen uns vor dem Bahnhof.
examples.en: We are meeting in front of the station.

examples.de: Nach dem Kurs fahre ich ins Zentrum.
examples.en: After the course, I am going into the city center.

examples.de: Sie fährt mit der Straßenbahn zur Arbeit.
examples.en: She takes the tram to work.

examples.de: Ohne einen Stadtplan finde ich das Museum nicht.
examples.en: Without a city map, I cannot find the museum.

commonMistakes.reason: 'Mit' requires the dative; masculine and neuter definite articles become 'dem'.
'Ohne' requires the accusative; a masculine indefinite article becomes 'einen'.

commonMistakes.wrong: Nach dem Kurs ich fahre nach Hause.
commonMistakes.correct: Nach dem Kurs fahre ich nach Hause.
commonMistakes.reason: The conjugated verb remains in position two when the prepositional phrase comes first.

specialCases: 'Vor dem Bahnhof' can mean spatially in front of the station, while 'vor dem Kurs' is temporal; context determines the meaning.
'Nach' also appears in destination expressions such as 'nach Berlin' and 'nach Hause'.
In spoken German, contractions such as 'im' for 'in dem' and 'vorm' for 'vor dem' are common; use standard forms when unsure.
tips: Color-code dative and accusative chunks instead of memorizing prepositions alone.
Practice each preposition with one city noun and one time expression.
Move the prepositional phrase to the front and check that the verb stays second.

memoryHooks.title: Mit brings dative company
memoryHooks.content: Whenever 'mit' brings someone or something along, bring a dative form too.

memoryHooks.title: Ohne removes an accusative object
memoryHooks.content: Picture 'ohne' taking something away in the accusative.
